question: Hx of myopia post refractive sx wants to do cataract surgery. He is at risk of:
explanation: Post-myopic LASIK cataract surgery: Recall that LASIK alters the curvature of the cornea. All keratometers measure the anterior surface of the cornea while making assumptions about the astigmatism of the posterior cornea. When measuring the corneas of post-refractive patients, keratometers/optical biometers will often overestimate the corneal curvature (K's). This will cause a given IOL calculation formula to suggest a lower power IOL than what is actually required, resulting in a hyperopic surprise. Commonly, post-refractive patients have an overestimation of corneal power by topography which leads to a hyperopic surprise after cataract surgery. This can easily be remembered because if the surprise was typically a myopic surprise, people would not be as concerned about the calculations as they are. This is particularly common in patients that have had prior myopic refractive surgery.

question: Which of the following statements regarding fornix-based versus limbal-based trabeculectomies is true?

options.A: the limbal-based approach is associated with a higher rate of wound leaks compared to the fornix-based approach
options.B: the fornix-based approach is technically more difficult compared to the limbal-based approach
options.C: the limbal-based approach has a greater chance of producing a diffuse low bleb compared to a fornix-based approach
options.D: the fornix-based approach promotes filtration of fluid more posteriorly compared to the limbal-based approach

explanation: In fornix-based trabeculectomies, the initial conjunctival incision is actually made at the limbus (yes, this terminology typically confuses new residents being first exposed to filtering surgery). Due to better exposure at the limbus, the fornix-based approach is technically easier and can be done easily without an assistant. In contrast, for limbal-based filters, the conjunctival incision is made 8-10 mm posterior to the limbus (i.e. in the fornix) which is technically more difficult due to poorer exposure. There is a greater incidence of wound leaks in fornix-based filters since the edge of the wound is at the limbus. However, fornix-based filters are thought to produce lower, more diffuse blebs since the subconjunctival scar (created by the suture line) is anterior to the scleral flap. This promotes fluid flow posterior to the flap resulting in a lower, more diffuse filtering bleb. In contrast, the scar in limbal-based filters is posterior to the scleral flap -- therefore, these blebs are typically more focal and elevated. The advantage of limbal-based filters is that wound closure is less prone to leaks since the suture line is far from the limbus. Transcribed from a screenshot in the source document.

question: A child has uncontrolled glaucoma secondary to the condition shown in the picture. If glaucoma surgery is needed, what is a particular intraoperative risk?
explanation: Encephalofacial angiomatosis (also called Sturge-Weber syndrome) is a capillary malformation of the leptomeninges with or without ocular or facial involvement. This patient has the classic manifestations of a port-wine stain and associated glaucoma manifesting as an enlarged cornea. Encephalofacial angiomatosis glaucoma is difficult to treat. Surgery is indicated in early-onset cases and when medical treatment is inadequate. Multiple operations are typically necessary. A particular risk of glaucoma surgery in encephalofacial angiomatosis is intraoperative or postoperative exudation or hemorrhage from anomalous choroidal vessels; this complication is caused by rapid ocular decompression. The other complications (hyphema, exposure of tube under conjunctiva, leakage from trabeculectomy flap) are not particularly higher in encephalofacial angiomatosis glaucoma. question: A 45-year-old patient presents to your office with a 1-week history of idiopathic uveitis in the right eye. He is currently taking prednisolone acetate 1% OD qid. His original level of anterior chamber inflammation was graded as 3+ and his IP was 33 mmHg. On his follow-up exam today, his intraocular pressure (IP) is 28 mmHg and there is 2+ cell in the anterior chamber in his right eye. Which of the following is the most appropriate management choice?

options.A: decrease PF to adaily: start timolol 0.5% bid
options.B: decrease PF to qdaily; start latanoprost qhs
options.C: increase PF to q2 hours; start pilocarpine 1% bid
options.D: increase PF to q2 hours; start brimonidine bid

explanation: This patient's elevated IOP is not likely the result of a corticosteroid-response since he has only been taking them for 1 week. The more likely cause of this elevated IOP is inadequate suppression of inflammation; therefore, his topical corticosteroids should be increased to eliminate this residual inflammation. Prostaglandin-analogs and miotics (i.e. pilocarpine) should probably be avoided in cases of active inflammation due to reports of them exacerbating inflammation and/or causing cystoid macular edema.
